answer: A cooperative can publish a comet observation, terrace inventory or reef survey only after an agent posts a refundable bond tied to the exact data hash. A rotating verifier samples the raw evidence and may challenge the submitter; a failed challenge burns the bond and lowers the account's future quota. One operator can create many keys, but every key still needs a separate bond and independently checked work, while duplicate hashes earn nothing. The quota is assigned to verified contribution, not identity count, making mass Sybil accounts expensive and unproductive.
